STEP 2 - Vessel: A square-ish white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: One bread slice, approximately 12 cm x 9 cm visible footprint. No butter, oil, or spread is visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The slice covers roughly 110 cm^2 of the plate, about 21% of the vessel area.

STEP 5 - Volume: 110 cm^2 x ~1.5 cm height (bread slice thickness, including crust and crumb envelope) ≈ 165 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bread-like slices use a bulk density of ~0.9-1.0 g/ml. Using 0.9: 165 ml x 0.9 ≈ 150 g. Bread slice of this size is plausibly 30-45 g for a standard slice, so I take the lower end given the visible thickness and open crumb: about 40 g.

Note on consistency: the volume-based estimate (150 g) is much higher than a typical bread slice, since the open, airy crumb holds far less mass than the envelope suggests. The bulk-density rule here is meant for dense items, so I weight the physical slice estimate more heavily.

STEP 7 - Energy: Bread, white/rustic, ~250-265 kcal per 100 g. Using 260 kcal/100 g: 40 g x 2.6 = about 104 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One slice of bread on a large plate is a small meal. About 40 g and roughly 100 kcal is plausible for what is visible. A full-volume estimate of 150 g would be too high for an airy slice of this kind.
